AFTER pds-w6-preflight-harness-fixes merges. ALSO AFTER pds-w6-charter-amendment and pds-w6-scratch-pointer-canonicalize merge. Do not start before all three are on origin/main: the first is the LAST legal edit to the instrument you are about to run and freeze, the second puts the decisions you must cite (D91-D111) where you can read them, the third stops your own cleanup stranding a pointer.

=================== WAVE-6 AMENDMENTS - these supersede everything below where they conflict ===================

(W6-A) THE EXPORT ROUTE IS /api/..., NOT /v1/... (PDS-D91). Three runs of GET /v1/workspaces/default/export returned HTTP 404 / 206 bytes. The real path is /api/workspaces/:workspace_slug/export (router.ex:2443), which the harness already uses at :580 and :1365 and which returns 200 / ~54.8 MB / 18 members. Any earlier brief text quoting /v1 for the export is WRONG - do not re-derive it, do not trust it.

(W6-B) CHECK-AND-GO, NEVER POUNCE (PDS-D92, PDS-D93). The direction that spawned this wave told you to watch for a deploy and pounce on the fresh BEAM. That is REFUTED and FORBIDDEN. Measured: MemAvailable was above the 2200 MB floor in 97 of 97 five-second samples across 486 s and in 52-73% of every 10-minute sample over four days, with a 130-minute continuous open window on the WORST day - the window is the box's majority state, not a knife edge. A deploy is worth mean +174 MB / median +146 MB with 9 of 30 NEGATIVE, and guerrilla is blue/green so a deploy is a memory TROUGH first (three coexisting BEAMs plus a live dep compile bottomed at 2248 MB). Worse, pouncing BREAKS gate (a) - DEPLOYED_SHA is pinned once at :562 - and step 0b, which hard-fails at :661 when the served sha is not an ancestor of your worktree. INSTEAD: just run it. A failed gate (b) returns at :1330 BEFORE the attempt counter increments at :1334, so a closed window costs ZERO attempts. If gate (b) is closed, wait ~10 minutes and run again. Record the MemAvailable reading in the transcript either way, and note PDS-D92's caveat: the gate is a point read taken ~60 s before the export peaks, and MemAvailable was observed swinging ~600 MB in 30 s under build load, so a pass at 2200-2400 MB is thin.

(W6-C) --all IS THE ONLY LEGAL SHAPE FOR ANYTHING TOUCHING RUNGS 2-6 (PDS-D101). canonical_order enforces ladder order only WITHIN one process; DEV_BUNDLE and PULL_BUNDLE are bash globals that do not survive a process boundary; step 6's guard-off control clobbers the target with no restore. --only 3,4 is FORBIDDEN. If 3/4 abort on headroom, the retry is a FULL --all, which re-imports the clobber, re-pins the sha, re-brackets step 8 and re-runs 6 AFTER 4 - and reuses a parked bundle for 0 attempts when the sha held (:1249-1261). THE DEFERRAL RULE: any deferral of 3/4 also defers 6.

(W6-D) ENV HYGIENE IS MECHANISM, NOT DISCIPLINE - GREP YOUR OWN TRANSCRIPT (PDS-D102). Before attempt 1: export PDS_CONTROL_PG=<maintenance conninfo> (an EXPORT, not a shell assignment - an unexported value prints 'instrument control: NOT RUN' and step 4 still reaches a terminal PASS, proven live); unset PDS_AMMO_FILE (an ambient value silently replaces the live 8-webhook ammo with whatever it names, proven live); leave PDS_STEP5_FAILDEMO and PDS_STEP6_GUARD_DEMO unset (both default 1). Then ASSERT, from the run's own output: the string 'instrument control: PASSED' appears and 'NOT RUN' does not, and the ammo line reads '8 webhook secret(s) pulled read-only from the source DB this run'. Note D80's headline was REFUTED - the literal bp-export-v1 reddens the DEV leg at exit 1; the genuinely dangerous shape is a STALE or PARTIAL real ammo file that is present in the full bundle but absent from dev and target, which passes all three legs while measuring almost nothing.

(W6-E) DO NOT EXTRAPOLATE RSS; CRITERION 9 IS UNMEASURABLE-BY-DESIGN ON AN ABORT (PDS-D103). A paired n=8 measurement of the cheap export gives 0.60x with a 95% CI of [-0.41x, +1.76x] - spanning zero - against PDS-D44's full-leg 2.53x: a 4.2x undershoot. The multiplier is regime-dependent (allocator slack absorbs 52 MiB and pays 897 MiB), so no multiplier carries between legs. The attempt counter and the RSS sampler both sit AFTER gate (b), so a headroom abort leaves NOTHING to report. If 3/4 abort, record criterion 9 as UNMEASURABLE-BY-DESIGN, not merely unmet. Also: the box's idle RSS alone swings 378 MiB over 135 s with zero requests, so any RSS number you do report needs its sampling rate stated (PDS-D104).

(W6-F) THE HEADLINE ENGINE FAIL IS ALREADY KNOWN - FILE IT, STATE IT, DO NOT FIX IT (PDS-D105). workspace_bundle.ex:259-276 holds every table's COPY bytes in one live dumps map; archive.ex:56-57 writes a temp tar and File.read!s it back into a second full-size binary while the first is still an argument; workspace_controller.ex:157 send_resp's it once, with no lock or semaphore near the route. ~2x-the-tar floor, ~1.9-2.2 GB for ONE request on a 3.9 GB box. A working chunked pattern already exists in the same tree (export_controller.ex:9-28). This belongs in the transcript as a first-class verdict WHETHER OR NOT 3/4 ever run, because it is the finding that outlives the run. Backlog task: pds-bl-streaming-workspace-export.

(W6-G) SINGLE OWNERSHIP IS ENFORCED AT /tmp (PDS-D106). FULL_ATTEMPTS_FILE and FULL_LOCK live at /tmp/pds-full-export (:125-129), machine-global and independent of BARKPARK_HOME - a second agent with a different home shares your budget, your lock and your parked bundle. Concurrent wave-6 activity WAS observed live (three unowned memory-watch loggers on guerrilla, fresh /tmp/pds-* artifacts from another session). Claim this bp task before touching the store, pin ONE BARKPARK_HOME and ONE PDS_SCRATCH_POINTER explicitly (never the defaults), and source $BARKPARK_HOME/scratch.env before teardown.

(W6-H) TWO CANDIDATE HOLES WERE EXAMINED AND DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. PDS-D109: step 3's full-bundle control leg lacks the dev leg's grammar guard, but its '> 0' polarity makes every garbage grammar fail closed at 0 (measured: CSV=0, JSON-lines=0, zero-byte=0, column-drift=0, honest COPY TEXT=1) - state in the transcript that the control is guarded by POLARITY, not by a grammar assertion, and that its failure message would misdiagnose a grammar change as an ammo problem. PDS-D110: step 5's PASS line does not self-declare a disabled FAILDEMO, but the default is 1 and acceptance criterion index 5 already disqualifies any transcript carrying 'failure demo DISABLED'. Neither is yours to fix - the harness is FROZEN from attempt 1 (PDS-D100).

(W6-I) FIRST-RUN COSTS, so a slow start is not mistaken for a hang. The Go bp build in ensure_bp is ~8-14 s on this host (warm machine-global GOCACHE) and is called exactly ONCE, in step 1 - --plan and 0a/0b/0c cost zero Go build. The minutes belong to pds-scratch-target.sh's TWO Elixir compiles: measured 3:11 cold under concurrent load, with the script's own header budgeting >10 min cold / ~90 s warm. Do NOT kill a live mix compile at minute 4.

(W6-J) THE DELIVERABLE AND ITS PUBLICATION PATH. File: scripts/pds-pull-proof.crown-transcript.txt, append-only (attempt 1's reds are NEVER deleted), with scripts/pds-pull-proof.first-run.txt retired in the same PR (PDS-D87). Note first-run.txt's banner is now a strict SUBSET of what the harness emits, so diffing against it yields false positives - capture your own banner. Then publish a Barkpark paper: the mutate body was proven live end to end (PDS-D108) - a batched [create, publish] against /v1/data/mutate/production with style=article, a description of at least 20 characters, and 1-12 registered weighted tags with DISTINCT strengths and rationales of at least 20 characters. bp doc create <type> --file - DOES honour stdin (a bare pipe without --file - is REFUSED, exit 2). Any patch mutation MUST carry 'type' or it returns 400 malformed. Choose a title that diverges from the six existing PDS paper titles - the dedup wall refuses at Jaccard 0.55 with 3+ shared tokens, and three prior rejections are on record for this epic.

(W6-K) THE BANNER'S HONESTY LINE, restated with what the evidence now supports. Open with: the served sha at start AND re-pinned at close (step 8 must actually RUN and print a verdict - an ABORT means an UNDATED transcript, per criterion 10); which plane ran; the measured RSS peak WITH its sampling rate, or an explicit UNMEASURABLE-BY-DESIGN; the env-hygiene evidence from (W6-D) quoted verbatim; and the exact scope of every claim - dev-profile table-DENY not field-scrub, content-and-presence not byte-identity, raw-perspective census EXCLUDING bare-slug E3 (pre-declared, PDS-D45), refusal scope limited to merge-import, and asset sizes compared against the TARGET's stored size. Every FAIL gets FILED as a task, never fixed away.

=================== END WAVE-6 AMENDMENTS ===================

AFTER pds-w5-criteria-reconcile AND pds-w5-harness-hygiene merge (WAVE-5 ROUND 2). Do not start before both are on origin/main: the first rewrites three of the criteria you are judged by, the second closes two holes in the instrument you are about to run. Branch from a freshly fetched origin/main in your OWN worktree — the primary checkout is 58 commits behind and does not contain scripts/pds-pull-proof.sh.

=================== WAVE-5 AMENDMENTS — these supersede everything below where they conflict ===================

(W5-A) THE FOUR DEPENDENCY PRs ARE MERGED. #4586 (harness rungs) / #4587 (--dataset CLI fix) / #4588 (guard eighth column) / #4589 (media size pin) merged 2026-07-19T22:24Z and all four merge commits are ancestors of origin/main. There is nothing to merge. The harness on main is 2244 lines, 11 rungs (0a 0b 0c 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8) plus --plan, with ZERO hardcoded ABORTs.

(W5-B) THE PREFLIGHT IS ALREADY PAID — do not re-spend it. A live --only 0a,0b,7,8 returned 4 PASS / 0 ABORT / 0 FAIL, pinning version=0.2.25.1330 sha=0b4c677fd, a 200 dev export of 53,932,544 bytes carrying profile=dev dataset=production, a live 403 bundle_import_disabled, and a step-8 re-pin on the SAME sha with uptime 1709 -> 1721. The full-export budget is genuinely UNSPENT (spent so far=0, on-disk bundle=absent) and the host holds no scratch pointer. The step-4 instrument control passes standalone end to end (CONTROL EXIT=0; FIRE 2 hits on the full bundle, FIRE 2 hits on the target DB, CLEAN 0 hits on the deny-shaped dev bundle, throwaway DB dropped). Step 4 ammo is live: the exact ssh+sudo-psql query returns 8 webhook secrets.

(W5-C) THE BUCKET RULE (PDS-D83) — sort every red BEFORE you touch anything. HARNESS BUG: fix the instrument, and show the corrected assertion still fails on the pre-fix condition. ENGINE FAIL: report it, file it as a task, do NOT fix it this wave. The most dangerous act available to you is editing the harness until a red goes away; that converts an engine FAIL into a vacuous green at exactly the moment it is most tempting. A FAIL in the transcript is the INTERESTING outcome and is never downgraded, re-run until green, or explained away.

(W5-D) THE CLOSING RULE, pre-declared (PDS-D84). This task closes ONLY if rungs 3 and 4 pass WITH their controls FIRING off the one full bundle AND rungs 1/2/5/6 pass against a real booted target. A severable headroom ABORT of 3 and 4 is an honest designed outcome and does NOT close this task — those two rungs are the exact leg the zero-secrets headline stands on. Anything less is a partial climb with the unpaid legs named.

(W5-E) TWO ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES DECIDE WHETHER RUNG 4 MEANS ANYTHING.
  export PDS_CONTROL_PG=postgres (or a fuller maintenance conninfo) in the SAME shell that invokes the harness. Step 4 gates its control on [ -n "${PDS_CONTROL_PG:-}" ] at L1648 and does NOT fall back to the bare postgres default the standalone scanner uses; without it the step prints "instrument control: NOT RUN" and still passes, and rung 4 cannot close (PDS-D79).
  unset PDS_AMMO_FILE for the climb. resolve_ammo() short-circuits on it with an early return before ssh_available (L1591-1594), REPLACING the SSH-derived webhook secrets. A leaked value makes all three of step 4's legs measure a literal string, printing three greens while proving nothing about webhooks.secret (PDS-D80).

(W5-F) THE DEPLOY EPOCH (PDS-D78). Deploy fires 58 times per 24h with a ~28.5 minute median and there is no quiet-window mechanism anywhere. Rung 0b asserts merge-base --is-ancestor DEPLOYED_SHA worktree_sha: tolerant of the worktree being ahead, FAILING two ways when the BOX is ahead (cat-file -e misses the object at L645-647, or is-ancestor is false at L655-657). A red 0b from a box-ahead is a DEPLOY-EPOCH EVENT: re-fetch, rebase the climb worktree, restart the run, and SAY SO in the transcript. It is NEVER an assertion to loosen. Print the epoch boundary; a differential straddling two binaries is reported as UNDATED, not as a result. Be aware a CI deploy run has been observed reporting SUCCESS without advancing the box, so the deploy may land at an unpredictable moment rather than on the median cadence.

(W5-G) FIRST-PASS RUNGS OWE A MUTATION (PDS-D81/D82). Keep PDS_STEP5_FAILDEMO=1 and PDS_STEP6_GUARD_DEMO=1 — a run that disables either says so in its own PASS line and does not satisfy criteria 6 and 7. Record demo status PER RUNG in the verdict table using the three honest classes: DEMONSTRATED BY DEFAULT (5, 6), DEMONSTRATED BUT SEVERABLE (3, 4 — their proof capability is itself conditional on the export), UNDEMONSTRATED PASSIVE (everything else, including step 2's ERR row and step 3's COPY-TEXT grammar check). Run these two proven mutations as SEPARATE throwaway invocations, never inside the climb:
  step 4 ammo poison: PDS_AMMO_FILE containing the literal bp-export-v1 (12 bytes, clear of MIN_AMMO_LEN=8; present in every real bundle because Archive.pack/2 calls erl_tar create with an EMPTY option list so nothing is compressed, and the scanner greps EXTRACTED members). It reddens step 4's PRIMARY dev-clean assertion at exit 1 and returns before the export-costing control, spending zero budget. SCOPE: it proves the extraction+grep plumbing and the HIT-to-FAIL conversion, NOT the dev partition's table DENY.
  step 1 cheap-fail: a nonexistent workspace slug exits 4 in ~0.09s with NO output file created. SCOPE: it proves step 1 converts a non-zero export exit into a FAIL; it is NON-DISCRIMINATING (a bogus token returns the byte-identical not_found envelope and identical exit 4) and it kills steps 2/5/6, so run it alone.

(W5-H) THE TRANSCRIPT IS A DURABLE, CITED RECEIPT (PDS-D87). Commit it as scripts/pds-pull-proof.crown-transcript.txt, append-only — attempt 1's reds are never deleted. DELETE scripts/pds-pull-proof.first-run.txt in the same PR: it is the pre-#4586 run (3 PASS / 7 ABORT / 0 FAIL, sha ec70fdc3d, no step 8, ABORT stubs for 1/2/5/6) and is cited by NO doc, card, paper or charter line across all 627 tracked .md files, so leaving it beside the real transcript means the stale one gets read as the crown proof. Then publish an evidence Paper (style=article, description of 20+ chars, 2-4 weighted registered tags) that cites the committed transcript path and this task id, and link it from the charter.

(W5-I) EXECUTION LAW. purpose.statement: Prove a full guerrilla dataset can be exported, imported into a clean scratch target, validated for counts/assets/secrets, and served correctly in one run.
purpose.why: The larger PDS goal is a dependable local development copy of real cloud state. Unit tests and partial exports could not prove that one production-shaped dataset survives the whole path without missing rows, broken assets, leaked secrets, or evidence borrowed from prior attempts. A frozen, budgeted crown climb was the right intervention because only one coherent run can establish composition across every subsystem. If omitted, the epic would claim a working dev loop from disconnected green fragments rather than a reproducible outcome.
